qAndA.answer: The video uses a time-lapse of a butterfly emerging from its chrysalis as a visual metaphor for transformation.

qAndA.answer: Barbara Stehle emphasizes that physical conferences provide 'materiality to the thought,' making it easier to understand and internalize ideas compared to reading about them.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of holding a physical conference, according to one of the speakers?

qAndA.answer: Janet Esquirol highlights the benefit of local conferences in creating and fostering a local network within a specific community.
qAndA.question: What is Janet Esquirol's main point about local conferences?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: When you set aside an entire day for new ideas, wonderful things happen.
The theme of TEDx Filton Street 2014 is the chrysalis, radical transformations.
We're giving you the opportunity to meet some of the creators who have shaped our world
in terms of technology, entertainment, and design.
The day is going to be broken into four sessions, fantasy, to reality,
secret passions, analog to digital, unexpected discoveries.
You think about the word media. It is something between you and the experience.
The wonderful thing of being at a conference physically is that it gives materiality to the thought
and it's always easier to understand it than having it in print.
The great thing about having a local conference is creating a local network.
From the old fish market to the New World Trade Center, Filton Street is the entrepreneurial
lifeblood of Lower Manhattan.
It's a meeting of entrepreneurs, innovators, architects, and artists, painters, writers,
composers, anyone who loves to create and has a passion for learning,
we're all going to join together for one day of cross-disciplinary experience.
If you could meet Plato, we could meet Einstein, it would make our day, wouldn't it?
If you have an opportunity to be present, I recommend that you do so.
Inspiration always comes from somewhere unexpected.
Make sure you come out.
Join us on June 10th for Ted X Filton Street.

youtube_description:
On June 10th, 2014, innovators in Technology, Entertainment, and Design will gather for a one-day conference in Lower Manhattan, for a day of creative collaboration and cross-disciplinary inspiration.  In this video, some of its organizers speak about who will be coming, and what it's all about.

This video was produced by Aaron Sylvan and directed by Janet Esquirol, with camerawork and editing by Sohee Kwon, audio and animation by Juan Rugero, and special thanks to Shutterstock for the monarch butterfly footage from http://footage.shutterstock.com/clip-1432093

TEDxFultonStreet is a not-for-profit, independently organized event, under contractual license from TED Conferences.  For additional information about the event, please visit http://TEDxFultonStreet.com and join the mailing list at http://bit.ly/tedxfultonstreet

Apply for tickets to our June 10, 2014 event: http://bit.ly/txf2014
